quarterly_data.signal: CTO Julie Eng said isolators - which protect the laser from unwanted back reflection that otherwise harms the performance of the link - are becoming a key component in the CPO and NPO ramp, and that Coherent has customers securing capacity for garnet and isolators with long-term agreements. Coherent is vertically integrated in garnet, the magneto-optic material isolators are based on: it grows the garnet boule in the U.S., slices it into substrates and polishes them, grows garnet epitaxy on top, dices them and attaches polarizers, and she said it supplies 'a significant fraction of the industry's garnet and isolators today'.

CTO Julie Eng described the external laser source (ELS) as an integration platform: Coherent combines the laser with its own coupling lenses, isolator, ELS fiber assembly and thermoelectric cooler (which keeps the laser at a constant temperature), all internal components it designs and manufactures before integrating them into the ELS, which she said lets it respond faster to customer specifications. The lenses that focus the light into the isolator and fiber are glass molded lenses for efficient light coupling, in production by the end of this calendar year; Coherent has shipped a quarter billion lenses across its lens portfolio. ELS assembly and test is built on Coherent's transceiver line, and Coherent is sampling ELSs to customers today.
quarterly_data.figure: ELS sampling to customers today; glass molded lenses in production by the end of this calendar year; a quarter billion lenses shipped

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Julie Eng said Coherent has had internal fiber design and manufacturing for 25 years and has shipped over 300 million meters of fiber, but it focuses only on hard-to-make specialty fiber and does not compete in standard commodity SMF or MMF. Its polarization-maintaining fiber - key for silicon photonics in the remote-laser CPO architecture - is production-ready now, and its multi-core fiber serves the highly dense VCSEL-array solutions for NPO, CPO and chip-to-chip. She said Coherent is executing 'a very significant fiber manufacturing expansion for both CPO and NPO'.
quarterly_data.figure: 25 years of in-house fiber; over 300 million meters shipped; very significant fiber manufacturing expansion for CPO and NPO

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Julie Eng said Coherent is introducing two products at ECOC 2026: a Mode-Matched Fiber that improves coupling efficiency to edge-coupled silicon photonics, and a detachable FAU (fiber attach unit) connector that helps with serviceability and installation.

CTO Julie Eng walked through the parts Coherent makes to couple light from the fiber into silicon photonics: microlens arrays lithographically formed in silicon (precisely uniform from one lens to the next), Prism Micro Lens Arrays that also turn the light for grating-coupled silicon photonics, and precisely V-groove-etched fiber guides that hold the fiber. It integrates these with its polarization-maintaining fiber into a fiber attach unit (FAU), and can integrate all the FAUs into a precision fiber assembly that routes and protects the fibers for ease of deployment and less fiber damage. She said all of these are either in production now, by the end of this year or early next year.
quarterly_data.figure: either in production now, by the end of this year or early next year

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Julie Eng said that once fiber inside the rack reaches very high amounts, reducing fiber count becomes very important to customers, and Coherent makes three in-production parts for it: circulators, which combine signals going in opposite directions onto the same fiber and reduce fiber count by a factor of 2 (built on garnet plus yttrium vanadate crystal, which Coherent also designs and manufactures internally); WDM multiplexers that combine many wavelengths, relying on super-precision optical coatings Coherent delivers at scale; and fiber shuffles that organize high-density fiber routing and help reduce fiber breakage. Circulators and WDM multiplexers can be placed in the fiber shuffle, in the ELS or in connectors.
quarterly_data.figure: circulators reduce fiber count by a factor of 2; all in production

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Julie Eng said Coherent has an in-house silicon photonics design team, uses multiple foundries (as is common in the silicon industry) and does assembly and test in-house; it has demonstrated 200G-per-lane silicon photonics and is shipping it in production in its transceivers today. At OFC in March of this year it demonstrated a 400 gigabit link based on silicon photonics, on the show floor and in a post-deadline paper, and she said Coherent is, to her knowledge, the only one in the world to have shown that.
quarterly_data.figure: 200G per lane silicon photonics in production; 400 gigabit silicon photonics link demonstrated at OFC

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Julie Eng detailed Coherent's 6.4T Silicon Photonics NPO module, shown at OFC and again at ECOC: it integrates silicon photonics modulators and photodetectors with drivers, TIAs and all the optical coupling in 32 lanes of 200G, and as a socketed NPO it delivers 15 gigabits per second per millimeter. It can be fed by a remote ELS through Coherent's FAU and precision fiber assembly or have the laser integrated into the silicon photonics NPO, and the same 6.4T silicon photonics provides the modulation and detection in Coherent's end-to-end CPO solution.
quarterly_data.figure: 6.4T; 32 lanes of 200G; 15 gigabits per second per millimeter

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Julie Eng presented Coherent's VCSEL-based NPOs. The VCSEL NPO shown at OFC integrates the VCSEL, photodiodes, drivers, TIAs and coupling optics into a single deployable NPO. The NPO built on the 2D VCSEL array integrates the substrates, drivers and TIAs, 2D VCSELs, 2D photodiode arrays, a heat spreader and a lens array, and has been demonstrated at 1.2 picojoules per bit, which she said is, as far as she knows, the lowest CPO or NPO power consumption including the laser. A second NPO built on the high-density VCSEL and photodiode, integrated with TIAs and drivers, can take the light out the top or out the side (adding a turning mirror, lenses and a lensed fiber array).
quarterly_data.figure: 1.2 picojoules per bit, including the laser

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Julie Eng laid out the CPO vs NPO trade-off: CPO puts the optical engine literally on the package of the switch or XPU chip and offers the lowest power consumption and, in many cases, the highest density, while NPO moves the optics off the package onto the board right next to it - easier to deploy and more serviceable, but moving it away from the chip costs power and the socket impacts signal integrity. NPO is also an architectural platform: a common form factor and socket can accommodate either silicon photonics or VCSELs, and Coherent is a founder of the Open CPX MSA, helping develop an open ecosystem for a common connector among vendors to give customers architectural flexibility.

CTO Julie Eng said interest in chip-to-chip optical interconnect has grown a lot in the last 3-9 months (this calendar year): as bandwidth between compute and memory scales, the optical link moves from the edge of the package to the interior of the package - after the intercontinental, terrestrial, data-center and now in-rack shifts from electronics to photonics, 'the next frontier, inside the chip package'. Customers are looking at multiple architectures, including an ELS with ultra-high-power lasers, integrated lasers and high-density VCSEL solutions, and with so many lanes there is a lot of discussion of WDM, making circulators and WDM multiplexers 'a very important architectural tool'.
quarterly_data.figure: interest up over the last 3-9 months

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Julie Eng said Coherent has shipped over 650 million of the optical components she introduced for the PhotonLink shape, guide and receive stages and is in high volume in all of them. She pitched the breadth of the portfolio as making Coherent a 'trusted advisor': because it has all the technologies, it can give a customer an honest assessment of each architecture (with VCSELs, the power consumption and cost; with an integrated laser, the complexity and the impact on signal integrity) instead of selling one solution, and she said Coherent is 'definitely scaling all of these technologies and products today'.

connects_to.relationship: CW laser sources and CPO solutions (high-power CW laser, ELS modules, fiber attach units) under multiyear supply agreement; NVIDIA made $2B equity investment in Coherent

contracts.signal: CTO Julie Eng identified the anchor customer long-term agreement (LTA) secured for Coherent's CPO solution as 'our NVIDIA agreement, which is a public agreement' - the only customer named at the PhotonLink launch - among over 10 active customer engagements in CPO. She expects CPO scale-out in Q4 of 2026 and scale-up in the second half of next year.
